dedupe_keys.name: catalonia semsim a sumo based simulator for locating ambulances of the emergency medical system

description: This case study presents SEMSIM, a simulation tool for testing where the ambulances of an emergency medical system should be stationed. Its name stands for Sistema d'Emergències Mèdiques SIMulator, after the Catalan emergency medical system, and it was built by researchers at the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, the University of Barcelona, Hospital Universitari Sant Joan de Reus and the Institut de Recerca Biomèdica Catalunya Sud. SEMSIM runs on the open SUMO traffic simulator and mimics how the service manages ambulances, so planners can compare alternative assignments of the available ambulances to existing bases, or add new base locations, and see the average response time of each configuration against the current one; the authors intend it to support configurations that change over time, for example by time of day. The article was published in 2025 in Emergency Medicine International and is free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is the Catalan service area studied. Caveats: the abstract does not report results for specific configurations, and the simulator code is not stated to be released. Simulation uses: a template for coupling traffic simulation with ambulance dispatch to evaluate base locations. Related records: the Lazio ambulance base simulation (case_study-lazio-ares-118-ambulance-location-des) and the Fez-Meknes deployment data (data-fez-meknes-ambulance-deployment) address the same problem elsewhere.
